data.title: Tesla Removes Unpopular Full Self-Driving Feature in Major V15 Update - TipRanks.com
data.summary: Electric vehicle maker Tesla (TSLA) has removed a mandatory feedback menu from its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system with the release of version 15. The update began reaching select customers on November 21 and includes several other improvements. Tesla also claims that the software reduces serious driver interventions by 25 times, although it has not released supporting data to verify that figure. [...] These changes are particularly important as Tesla works to grow its FSD business. The company reported 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of September, up by 67% from a year earlier. Tesla currently offers FSD through a $99 monthly subscription in the U.S., although the software still requires drivers to pay attention and be ready to take control. [...] For now, version 15 is available to a limited number of vehicles that are equipped with Tesla’s newer Hardware 4 computer. CEO Elon Musk expects a wider release in December as part of the company’s annual holiday software update. What Is the Prediction for TSLA Stock?

data.title: Tesla’s Driver-Assistance Software Now Looks Like a Video Game
data.summary: Tesla is rolling out the 15th iteration of its Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software, and the update comes with some pretty impressive graphics. It’s called Tesla Reality View, and it’s exactly that, using the vehicle’s cameras to record what’s going on around you, then re-create the scene on the central screen accurately. [...] - Tesla’s latest update for its driver-assistance software includes a huge graphical upgrade. - Called Reality View, it shows a realistic rendering of cars, buildings, and people around your Tesla. - There are also a number of upgrades to the assistance software, including an improved ability to react to potholes and small animals. [...] Users’ experiences since the rollout have indicated that V15 appears to be more cautious in certain situations, and in some cases a little overcautious. Posts on Reddit’s Tesla forum report a vehicle aggressively avoiding random items in the road and reacting to a road repair site as if it was a pothole. Other forum users point out that early FSD updates often are a little shaky right at rollout but more polished by the time the release goes out more broadly.
